name: Saint Teresa Benedicta of the Cross
history: Edith Stein, a brilliant Jewish philosopher, found the truth she had long sought in reading the life of Saint Teresa of Ávila and was baptised in 1922. She became a Carmelite nun in Cologne. In 1942 she was arrested in the Netherlands and killed at Auschwitz. She is a co-patron of Europe.
life: Edith Stein was born in Breslau on the Day of Atonement, 1891, the youngest child of a devout Jewish family. As a young woman she lost her faith, studied philosophy and became the assistant of Edmund Husserl. In 1921, staying with friends, she read the autobiography of Saint Teresa of Ávila through the night and, closing it, knew that it was the truth. She was baptised on 1 January 1922. For years she taught at a Dominican school in Speyer, lectured widely and wrote on women and education. Barred from teaching by the Nazi laws of 1933, she entered the Carmel of Cologne that year. In 1938 she was moved to Echt in the Netherlands for safety. After the Dutch bishops publicly condemned the deportation of Jews, the Nazis arrested Catholics of Jewish origin, and on 2 August 1942 Edith and her sister Rosa were taken. She died in the gas chamber at Auschwitz on 9 August. John Paul II canonised her in 1998.
prayerTo: Saint Teresa Benedicta, you sought the truth with your whole mind and found it in Christ crucified. Pray for all who search, for the Jewish people you loved, and for Europe, whose patron you are. Help me to embrace the cross that comes to me and to stand with those who suffer. Amen.
penance: Pray today for the Jewish people and for all victims of hatred, and give an hour to serious reading that will help you understand your faith more deeply.
meditation: As she was taken, Edith is remembered to have said to her sister, Come, we are going for our people. For whom is God asking you to stand today?
